chess/classic.checkYou: Check! Your turn — defend or counterattack.
chess/classic.heroDesc: A dark chess lab. Pick a side, outplay the bot, deliver mate, and hold the position.
chess/classic.heroTitleHtml: Hack the board. Capture the flag.
chess/classic.rulesHtml:
• Goal: checkmate the opponent’s king.
  • Pieces: the rook moves in straight lines, the bishop on diagonals, the queen either way, the knight in an L, the king one square.
  • Turns: White starts. You may not leave your own king in check.
  • Check and mate: check must be answered; checkmate ends the game.
  • Special moves: castling, en passant, and pawn promotion.
  • Draw: stalemate, repetition, insufficient material, or agreement.

chess/custom.heroDesc: A dark chess lab. Pick a side, outplay the bot, deliver mate, and hold the position.
chess/custom.heroTitleHtml: Hack the board. Capture the flag.
chess/custom.rulesHtml:
• Setup: before the game you place pieces on an empty or standard board.
  • Palette: pick a piece (white or black), then a square to place it. Clicking the same piece again removes it; a different piece replaces it. A second king of the same color cannot be placed (at most one white and one black king).
  • Start: you need exactly one white king and one black king. If the side to move is already mated, you get a warning, but you may still start.
  • Play: from there it is classic chess — Stockfish, side choice, online rooms.
  • Multiplayer: the setup syncs (FEN); both players confirm the start, or the host starts when the position is ready. Spectators only watch.

chess/dice.checkYou: Check! Your turn — defend or counterattack.
chess/dice.heroDesc: A dark chess lab. Pick a side, outplay the bot, deliver mate, and hold the position.
chess/dice.heroTitleHtml: Hack the board. Capture the flag.
chess/dice.mpPlayingHint: Move your piece. The bot is off.
chess/dice.rulesHtml:
• Goal: checkmate; in this mode capturing the king also ends the game.
  • Roll: at the start of a turn roll 1–3 dice: 1 pawn, 2 knight, 3 bishop, 4 rook, 5 queen, 6 king.
  • Moves: make one move of each type you rolled; doubles mean several moves of that type.
  • Limit: you may move only the types you rolled. A type with no move is skipped; if nothing can move, the turn passes.
  • Chess rules: normal moves, captures, and pawn promotion still apply.

chess/atomic.rulesHtml:
• Capture: a capture removes the capturing piece, the captured piece, and every piece within one king-step of the capture square — except pawns (pawns do not explode).
  • King: if a king is in the blast, that side loses. A move that explodes your own king while the opponent’s king survives is illegal.
  • Mate: the king is threatened by explosion or capture and there is no legal move.
  • Bot: a local search under atomic rules (not Stockfish).
  • Multiplayer: create a room or join with a code; spectators are welcome.

chess/knights.checkYou: Check! Your turn — defend or counterattack.
chess/knights.rulesHtml:
• Setup: kings and pawns as in classic chess; every other piece is a knight of the same color.
  • Moves: knights move in an L; pawns and the king move as usual. There is no castling (no rooks).
  • Goal: checkmate or capture the king.
  • Bot: Stockfish on the knight-army FEN.
  • Multiplayer: create a room or join with a code; spectators are welcome.

checkers/classic.rulesHtml:
• Man: moves diagonally forward.
  • Forced capture: you may jump forward or backward. If several chains exist, pick any.
  • King: moves and jumps any distance along a diagonal.
  • Series: keep capturing while another jump is available.
  • Win: the opponent has no pieces or no moves.

checkers/custom.customSettingsHostOnly: Only the room creator can change settings before the start
checkers/custom.customSettingsLocked: Settings are locked until the game ends
checkers/custom.rulesHtml:
• Base: Russian draughts on 8×8, flying kings.
  • Backward capture: on — men jump forward and backward (Russian style); off — forward only (international style).
  • Forced capture: on — you cannot make a quiet move when a jump exists; off — a quiet move is allowed.
  • Move timer: off / 10 / 30 / 60 / 120 sec. Running out of time loses for the side to move.
  • Multiplayer: only the room creator edits settings before the first move; if the opponent leaves, play continues against the bot.
checkers/custom.setBackwardHint: On — men jump backward (Russian); off — forward only
checkers/custom.setMandatoryHint: Off — you may move without capturing even if a jump exists

chess/three.rulesHtml:
A short paraphrase of the 96-cell hexagonal board — from the Wikipedia article “Chess for three” (the rules section in the spirit of Robert Zubrin’s board). Not a verbatim quote.

  • Players. Three sides: White, Red, and Black. Each has a camp and a normal set of 16 pieces. The first move is drawn by lot; after that, turns pass clockwise.
  • Board. A hexagon of three camps. Lines bend where camps meet: rooks follow ranks and files, bishops follow diagonals, the queen does both, the knight jumps two squares and then one and leaps over pieces, the king steps to a neighboring square.
  • Pawns. They move forward along their file and capture diagonally. The left-hand pawns advance toward the player on the left, the right-hand pawns toward the player on the right; at the center seam a pawn can capture on three squares. From the starting square a pawn may move two steps. On the far rank of an enemy camp it becomes a queen. There is no en passant.
  • Check. You may not leave your king under attack. This version has no castling.
  • Checkmate. A mated player’s king is removed. The rest of that army stays and is taken over by the player who gave mate. From then on that player moves one piece of either color per turn, and the two armies cannot capture each other. Play continues until only one player still has a king — that player wins.
  • Stalemate. The article does not cover it. Here a stalemated player is eliminated and their pieces are removed; the others play on.
  • At the table. Sit as one color against two bots, or pass the device around three people.
